{"edits": [], "notes": "No edits proposed. The original finding (app/api_errors.py:10, `@validator`) is already resolved in the current content: `CreateUser.no_spaces` uses `@field_validator("username")` with `@classmethod`, and the import is correct. Nothing else in the finding needs changing.

The remaining test failure (tests/test_api_errors.py::test_codes) is a real v2 behavior change that is not covered by the findings. Pydantic v2 changed the error message text, and MESSAGE_CODES matches on case-sensitive `startswith` prefixes written for v1 text:
- "field required" -> v2 is "Field required" (capital F)
- "value is not a valid integer" -> v2 is "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer"
- "ensure this value has at least" -> v2 is "String should have at least N characters"

So every error falls through to "INVALID", which is what the test output shows. The fix is to update the MESSAGE_CODES keys (around lines 18-23) to the v2 prefixes "Field required", "Input should be a valid integer", and "String should have at least". Matching on err["type"] ("missing", "int_parsing", "string_too_short") would be more robust, but that also means changing the lookup line (around line 32). Both edits were rejected by the scope check because they are not near the @validator finding or the imports. I did not try to get them through by attaching them to unrelated lines, since that would misrepresent what they change. To fix the test, the scope gate needs to allow edits to the MESSAGE_CODES block and the error_codes lookup, or those findings need to be listed explicitly. Once that is approved, the edits are small and mechanical."}
